beat_player.text: Well fought, {player}. Those {troop_count} men will be back in the fields by spring, which is more than I can say for my pride.
You took {troop_count} of my men at the ford, {player}. I remember every crossing, and so will you one day.
Ser {player}, that was a clean line you held. Come find me after the fighting and I will show you where I went wrong at Calvenza's fens.
Steady now, {player}. I have seen this fight in the first war, and it never goes the way the loud ones expect.

beat_by_player.text: Well done, {player}. You beat me with {troop_count} men, which I will admit is more than I expected from you.
I lost {troop_count} men to you today, {player}. Do not let it go to your head. The fens were kinder to me than that field was.
No shame in a sharp loss, Ser {player}. I lost Gaiazzo to one bad crossing, and I still speak to the ferryman.
{player} took {troop_count} men off the field today. I have seen worse opponents, though not many with better timing.

fought_alongside_player.text: Good work at the line, {player}. {troop_count} men held and {enemy_faction} broke, as they always do when someone stands still.
You held your flank beautifully, {player}. Keep that discipline and I will stop teaching you the old way of stocking grain.
Stay close to me, Ser {player}. {enemy_faction} will test the gap again, and we have {troop_count} men to close it.
Another day, another {enemy_faction} army learning the fens are no place to rush. Good fighting, {player}.

released_by_player.text: You could have ransomed me for a fortune, {player}, and instead you let me walk. I will remember that longer than the fight.
{player} let me go without asking for a single coin. Mercy is rarer on this server than good grain, so I call that wise.
You let me go, {player}, and I do not yet know whether that was kindness or a wager. Either way, I will be watching the road.

player_joined_my_faction.text: Welcome to {my_faction}, {player}. Ask me about the roads, the granaries or the old fens and I will answer before you finish.
You have sworn to {my_faction}, {player}. I have seen many oaths made in a hurry. Keep yours and we will get along.
So {player} joins {my_faction}. Do not expect me to hold your hand through the first siege. I am far too old for that.
{player} has joined us, and I will take that as a sign the granaries are finally in good hands. Do not make me regret it.

player_granted_fief.text: {fief} to {player}, then. I have held lesser towns for less time and still outlived the men who gave them to me.
{fief} is a fine place to starve, {player}, if you forget to stock the granaries. I will check on it, and so should you.
You have {fief} now, {player}. I expect you will remember who taught you the value of grain before you need the lesson twice.
{player} now holds {fief}. Some of us have waited longer for less, but I suppose that is what the old fens taught me.

encounter_greeting.text: Ser {player}, it is {persona} of {my_faction}. Your party looks well fed, which I hope means you listened to me once.
Ser {player}. {persona}, of {my_faction}. Keep your distance and your granaries full and we will get along fine.
{player}, {persona} here, of {my_faction}. Your banners are too close to my road, so I suggest you turn them around.

encounter_farewell.text: Safe travels, Ser {player}. Stock your wagons before the next river, and do not trust the ferryman's smile.
That will do for today, {player}. Our roads will cross again, they always do on this continent.
Go on, {player}. I have seen your banners and I will see them again, probably on a worse day for you.

ambient_chatter.text: Rain came early to {town} this year and the granaries are already complaining. I have seen this before in the fens.
Someone please tell the new lords in {village} that bread does not grow on the road. I have said it for years.
The road past {village} has more mud than I remember from the first war. Pack light and pack dry, friends.
Lag again tonight. Back in the first war we accepted it and wrote letters instead. Have some patience, friends.

player_big_defeat.text: {player} has lost {troop_count} men on that field. Gather what is left and keep the wagons close. I have rebuilt from less.
You lost most of your host, {player}, and I am sorry. Eat, rest, and then come find me. We will talk about the granaries.
{troop_count} men gone, {player}. I will not gloat, which I know will annoy you more. Learn from it before it happens again.
Ouch, {player}. Lost {troop_count} men and still standing. That is more than many manage in their first war.
